A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Linear Bandits with Partially Observable Features. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–G are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic bandit experiments in Section 6, with cumulative-regret results in Figures 2–3 and trial details in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulation results, including comparisons of the two RoLF variants with four baseline algorithms.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2 and 5.1 change the resampling-cap denominator from log(1/p) to log(1/(1-p)), reducing the specified maximum trials. Feature augmentation, estimator objectives, and the pseudocode of Algorithms 1–2 otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three partially observed feature-space cases and two fully observed cases. Appendix D's time-varying-feature extension remains theoretical; no new evaluated dataset or task is introduced.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain LinUCB, LinTS, DRLasso, and UCB(delta) as baselines, alongside RoLF-Lasso and RoLF-Ridge. Comparator membership in Figures 2–3 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B retain the same reported simulation protocol: K = 30, T = 1200, p = 0.6, delta = 0.0001, feature-generation distributions, SVD processing, and scenario-specific dimensions. No experimental protocol revision is reported.

E4.justification: The comparisons across observability and feature-space relationships are retained. Neither version adds or removes an ablation, sensitivity test, robustness experiment, or empirical case study.

E5.justification: Appendix B specifies five independent trials with different random seeds and reporting of sample means and one standard deviation in both versions. The theoretical probability-bound revisions concern T1.

E6.justification: The five simulation panels in Figures 2–3 have identical curves and error bars. Their reported rankings, cumulative-regret trends, and qualitative experimental findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 removes the outer expectation from the regret definition. Theorem 2 changes its probability statement from per-round 1 - 2 delta/t^2 to an all-round 1 - 3 delta guarantee. Theorems 3 and 5 revise finite-time constants and logarithms, with corresponding derivation and probability-accounting changes in Appendix E. Appendix G.1 corrects the concavity statement to include the trace. The theorem coverage and leading regret rates are retained.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain feature augmentation plus doubly robust estimation, regret of order sqrt((d + dh)T) up to logarithms, operation without latent-feature knowledge, and empirical superiority over the retained baselines. The abstract's revised description of dh restates subspace dependence already discussed in v2.

C2.justification: The substantive explanations involving subspace overlap, forced exploration, variance control, and baseline failures are retained. Applicability discussions, the time-varying-feature extension, and future directions introduce no new limitation or interpretation.

D1.justification: The documented maximum-resampling instruction changes in the main text. Section 4.2 also adds an explicit epsilon-greedy probability description, but reverses the probabilities given in unchanged Algorithm 1. Appendix B's implementation settings and resource-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning are unchanged. Additional inline mentions of Ghosh et al. and Kim et al. reuse works and relationships already discussed elsewhere in v2.

P1.justification: v3 makes grammatical edits and localized rewrites of the abstract, method explanations, and proof prose. Section 4.2 moves the variance and resampling explanation after the pseudo-reward formula. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 adds the observed-component superscript to estimator labels and revises its caption. Several proof equations receive expanded displays and numbering, causing appendix reflow. Tables 1–2 and the experimental figure designs are retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting missing factors of two in Theorem 3 and the trace-concavity statement in Appendix G.1, together with more explicit proof steps, modestly improves mathematical precision. Empirical support is unchanged. The gain is limited by the new epsilon-greedy prose, which assigns the greedy action probability t^(-1/2), conflicting with Algorithm 1's retained probability 1 - t^(-1/2).
